reviews.title: Great Player, But It Needs Better Music Library Features
reviews.text:
I’ve been using VLC on iPhone as my primary offline music player, and it’s stable and reliable. However, there are several features that would make it much better for users with large music libraries.

1. The music library order changes by itself. Every few weeks, the order of my songs changes even though I haven’t modified my files. Please make the library order stable and predictable.
2. Please add more sorting options, including:
    * Date Added
    * File Creation Date
    * File Modification Date
    * Import Order
    These sorting methods are essential for users who regularly add new music and want their newest songs to appear at the top.
3. Please add a Favorites feature. Being able to mark songs as favorites and access them from a dedicated playlist would greatly improve the music experience.
4. Please improve music library management. Users with large offline collections (thousands of songs) need more powerful organization and browsing tools.
5. Please preserve the selected sorting method permanently. VLC should remember the user’s preferred sorting option and never change the order automatically.

VLC is already one of the best free media players on iOS. Adding these features would make it an excellent offline music player as well.

Thank you for your amazing work!

reviews.title: Poor UI, Poor Developer Logic
reviews.text:
I was looking forward to making VLC my default audio player, but I simply cannot. I spent absolutely ages trying to work out why the player does not resume playing audio tracks from the last played point. Then I came across this comment buried within a developer’s comment to a review: “ Is the audio file a podcast or longer than 30min? Otherwise, VLC will not remember the last playback position as users usually do not want that for their music.” The user wants exactly the same thing as I want - for the player to resume playing audio track. This arbitrary duration of 30mins is utterly ludicrous! It doesn’t hurt VLC developers to enable this for tracks under 30mins. This is inexplicable. People listen to all types of audio e.g. meeting minutes, lectures, interviews, memos, documentaries, etc. All of these can be under 30 minutes. What a ridiculous, unnecessary restriction. All it does it provide users with a reason to stop using VLC. Well done. Slow hand clap. 

Please, please, please address this ASAP and improve the decision-making that is undermining a good app. 

Thank you.

reviews.title: great player - problem with thumbnails.
reviews.text:
This video player has been my go-to for years, both on iPad and PC. It hurts to give 1 star. But this seems to be the *only* way to get through to developers. This is incredibly frustrating. 

For about a year thumbnails are not being recreated for certain videos. The experience is sporadic. Once one video fails, all subsequent videos fail to recreate the thumbnail. It’s not due to available space. I have force-closed the app several times, I have rebooted the device many times.

I understand this might be due to Apple’s sandboxing. I have 3 solutions:
1) do not delete the previous thumbnail until a new one has successfully been created.
2) offer the option to manually select a frame as a thumbnail. Once selected it is never changed.
3) offer the option in the settings to recreate thumbnails for all videos that are lacking a thumbnail.

Any of these are better than seeing a “play” symbol. I will return my review to 5* once this issue has been resolved.

reviews.title: Playback got worse after update - Please fix music folder issue
reviews.text:
I’ve been using VLC media player every day, especially in my car, and it used to be perfect for playing my music. But after the recent update, the music playback experience got much worse.

Before, I could just press play and it would instantly open my music folder and start playing all my songs. Now, when I press play, nothing opens automatically. I have to manually go through folders every single time, find my music folder, select all the files, and then press open just to start playback.

This is really inconvenient and honestly frustrating for daily use. It completely breaks the smooth experience the app used to have.

I’ve also seen similar issues mentioned by other users where playback from local files became unreliable or changed after updates (App Store).

Please fix this and bring back the old behavior where pressing play automatically opens and plays the music folder. This app is amazing otherwise, but this issue makes it much harder to use.

reviews.title: Pretty bad, but not because of the developer
reviews.text: This app is a sad shadow of the greatness it provides on pretty much every other platform. I don’t fault the devs though. Apple does everything they can to make apps locked down for security, but this means that some basic functionality is near impossible to provide on iOS. Want to load files from a local downloads directory? Good luck! It may or may not let multiple files open and play in order. Want to keep audio playing with the screen off? Well, the current file might finish playing (and even this isn’t certain), but expect wake up your device to manually reopen files you’d previously selected to play. Want to skip to the next track? Well it might skip every once in a while, but more likely, it will fast forward about 2 seconds of the current track. Seems to work slightly better on iPad, but an absolutely infuriating experience on iPhone.
